verified_local_mechanism.phenomenon: Large continuous action and future-force amplitudes at recorded late seed17 states
verified_local_mechanism.intervention: Only clip valid P2 raw-force-history entries to calibration-bound source marginal channel ranges; hold normalized P1 proprio, images, text, mask and all three initial noise draws fixed
verified_local_mechanism.specificity: Single wrist-fz clipping and complementary other-five clipping leave substantial motion/action amplification at frames143/207. P1 remains unchanged and saturated; it is not necessary to change P1 to remove the large amplification at these fixed observations.
verified_local_mechanism.mechanism_link: Unbounded calibrated history enters a linear projection; residual blocks retain the input path, and cross-attention normalizes action queries but not force keys/values before residual injection. Source linkage is consistent with observed input-path causal effects, not a measured layer-by-layer attribution.
verified_local_mechanism.negative_controls: Exactly identical initial observation under two protocol-noise groups has zero changed history entries and bit-exact raw action/future-force after clipping. A force-OOD seed11 frame98 without large gripper amplitude also changes under clipping, ruling out a claim that OOD alone is sufficient or clipping affects only failures.
limitations: Marginal source-range clipping is an offline amplitude intervention, not a joint-distribution or deployment-safety guarantee.
Future force remains above some source ranges even after clipping.
Clipped frame159 retains two early gripper reversals.
No task-success, grasp, release or stable-in-bin improvement has been demonstrated.
The mechanism explains late amplification, not yet why the original trajectory entered abnormal contact.

force_interface_saturation_cpu.claim: The deployed seed17 force inputs are far outside the training support; P1 (proprio force columns) is clamped to 5 sigma after normalisation and P2 (16-frame raw-newton history) is fed unclamped at hundreds of sigma.
force_interface_saturation_cpu.P1_mechanism: dims 8..13 = raw6 - zero_load_ref_median, then the v1g min/max normaliser whose force bounds are (-sigma,+sigma), i.e. residual/sigma32, clamped to [-5,+5].
force_interface_saturation_cpu.P2_mechanism: raw6 -> ForceHistoryEncoder.normalize = (raw - mean_raw)/std * 1.0, no clamp. mean_raw/std come from the same calibration file.

training_source_range_P1_sigma.note: pad_inner/pad_outer never exceed 2.27 sigma anywhere in the 42681-row corpus; only wrist fy/fz cross 5 sigma in 300/320 rows.

force_interface_saturation_cpu.downstream_mechanism: force_condition.py keeps the raw amplitude on the residual trunk (_CausalResidualBlock) and does not normalise the cross-attention force K/V, so P2's hundreds-of-sigma history can inject large magnitudes; P1's clamp destroys pad amplitude information by pinning it to a constant 5.
limits: A saturated input is a measured interface fact, not proof that it caused any action.
The P1 clamp is applied after normalisation in the model normaliser; the exact call site is action_norm_identity40k.py:82 and has not been re-derived for this file.
The P2 ring buffer feeds raw newtons; the model normalises internally, so the 500-sigma value reaches the encoder unless the model itself guards it (it does not).
No intervention was run here; whether the model response changes is still open.
Saturation is a measured interface fact; it does not by itself prove causation of contact onset or gripper reversals.

force_action_observational_coupling_cpu.claim: Within the recorded seed17 action stream, force-history peak and model-output action amplitude co-vary strongly in the same frame and the recorded executed chunks sit inside the amplified regime, so the amplification is not a re-inference artifact.
force_action_observational_coupling_cpu.counterexample: i350 has pad=0 but wrist fz=-88.2 N and raw absmax still 15.25, so wrist force alone can sustain amplification.
limits: Observational only: contact, state and images co-vary.
Raw model rows are the recorded executed-chunk outputs; rows 10..31 were never executed.
Adapter saturation is a command saturation, not a measured motion.

v5_counterfactual_plan_semantics_cpu.claim: Replaying the v5 clip counterfactuals through the identified de-normaliser and adapter shows a dose-response in time: at pre-contact f60 clipping changes nothing, while at f64/f70/f143/f159 it changes translation signs, saturation rows and gripper commands.
v5_counterfactual_plan_semantics_cpu.rotation_caveat: The adapter rotates the world rotation vector by R^T before scaling; no recorded EEF rotation is replayed here, so rotation dims 3..5 are only amplitude-mapped and their signs are not compared.

f60_precontact.interpretation: No history entry was out of source range yet, so the clip is a null operation; this is the temporal specificity control.

v5_counterfactual_plan_semantics_cpu.interpretation: These are offline predicted-plan comparisons. A sign disagreement says the plans diverge, not that either plan or the clipped policy is correct or safe.
limits: Offline arithmetic; a sign flip here says the two predicted action plans differ, not that either would succeed.
The adapter gripper rule is -sign(pm1); raw->pm1 uses the model binarisation.

The clean criterion test is the oracle run (arm parked at the reset pose), where 10 ideal placements stay exact_fill for 60 steps. A clean correction test must retract the arm first.
placement_counterfactual_v2_20261118.bin_stability: target bin is a free joint body but moves only 1.4 mm over the whole episode (reset 0.095,0.100,0.74978 -> final 0.09468,0.09862,0.74973), so the criterion frame is not drifting
placement_counterfactual_v2_20261118.verdict_provisional: height alone is not sufficient; horizontal correction is necessary; the post-release dynamics inside the bin need the arm-out-of-the-way test

placement_oracle_ABCDE_20261118.scope: oracle counterfactual on the real CL seed17 final state (qpos/qvel from placement_counterfactual_20261118_v2/final_state.npz); bodies moved directly, NOT policy execution

D C plus arm retraction.note: identical to C: the arm left in place does not disturb the placed plates

placement_oracle_ABCDE_20261118.slot_assignment: global linear_sum_assignment between the 13 moved cookies and the 10 slots, 10 distinct slots used
key_findings: arm interference is ruled out: C equals D at t0/20/60
height or horizontal correction alone is not enough, both together place 10 plates and they stay
the only reason C/D fail exact_fill is source_count 69 instead of 70: one plate was lost outside both bins
returning that single stray plate to the source makes strict exact_fill true for the full 20-step hold window
the criterion is therefore satisfiable from the real failure state with a finite correction; it is not an impossible task

slip_physics_verification_20261118.method: per let-go event, read the six calibrated force channels: pad_inner/pad_outer load in the 10 frames before, pad collapse in the 5 frames after, wrist force magnitude before/at the event; thresholds pad_loaded 1.0 N, pad_collapse 0.3 N, collision 50 N or 5x the pre window
slip_physics_verification_20261118.correction_of_earlier_claim: the earlier "about half of the moved plates slip while the command is closed" was based on EEF proximity alone. With pad-force evidence only 1-2 events per arm are confirmed physical slips; several "carried" plates never loaded the pads at all (dragged, not clamped). Intentional opens remain the dominant mode.

release_gate_G_20261118.design: P2-clamped arm plus one rule: whenever the model commands open while the EEF is outside |x-0.095|<=0.045, |y-0.100|<=0.045, z<=0.80, the command is replaced by close; 40-step continuous-gating cap and 150 N wrist-force suspension
release_gate_G_20261118.verdict: falsified in this form. The gate also fires during the approach, so the fingers are forced closed before the grasp; no plate ever leaves the source (source count stays 80) and the EEF never comes closer than 75-78 mm to the bin centre. It is not evidence that release gating cannot work, only that the gate must be conditioned on an actual grasp.
release_gate_G_20261118.next_design: carry-only gate: apply the open-block only while a plate is actually held, i.e. gripper commanded closed AND pad force > 1 N AND measured opening < 0.6; pass through otherwise; same window and protection.

early_release_vs_trajectory_20261118.question: is the policy releasing early on a correct transport, or never generating a bin-reaching endpoint?
early_release_vs_trajectory_20261118.method: for each arm take the first open command that follows a closed run >=10 steps (a real release), then measure the minimum EEF distance to the bin centre over the rest of the episode and over the whole episode
early_release_vs_trajectory_20261118.reading: two distinct mechanisms: in s17/s21 the EEF does later come within 19-25 mm of the bin centre, but only at frames 300-430, long after the early release - so delaying the release is a plausible fix there. In s11 the EEF never comes closer than 101 mm in the whole episode, so its transport endpoint itself is wrong and a release gate cannot help.

release_gate_G2_20261118.design: carrying state machine confirmed from past observations (previous chunk ended closed, pad>1 N, opening<0.6, twice); only in CARRYING are new open requests evaluated; release allowed when the carried cookie is over the box (inner half + 0.02) and its bottom is <= 0.06 bin-local; 40-step cap and 150 N suspension
release_gate_G2_20261118.reading: the state machine works and the grasp phase is preserved (no lost events, source still falls to 71, same force as CL), but the outcome equals CL s21. The gate allowed 36 releases because its test (inner+0.02, bottom<=0.06) is looser than the sim criterion (inner+0.004, bottom within [-0.003,+0.004] of the floor). At most open moments the cookie was already roughly over the box, so release timing is not the binding factor in s21; placement precision is.
release_gate_G2_20261118.next: G3 uses the exact sim criterion at release (tolerance 0.004 and bottom within [-0.003,+0.004]); if the 40-step cap is hit, log rather than release. If G3 still yields zero, pivot to grasp/transport endpoint and placement geometry rather than further gate tuning.
release_gate_G2_20261118.seed17_reading: first non-zero in-target count in a real policy run (1 plate), but accompanied by a 4373 N pad-channel spike; exact_fill still false; single seed, not a validated fix

g2_spike_forensics_20261118.context: opening 0.579->0.455 in one step at f128; pads steady 27-29 N and gripper force 58 N at f118-127; wrist 90-101 N then 31 N; grip command alternated +1/-1 because the gate blocked open requests at f110 (19 rows) and f120 (25 rows)
g2_spike_forensics_20261118.gate_reason: blocked because the carried cookie sat at bin-local y=0.135 (over_box False) while low=True
g2_spike_forensics_20261118.why_guard_missed: the 150 N guard only tested wrist channels 0:2; the spike is on pad_outer (ch13) and the wrist read 30.8 N
g2_spike_forensics_20261118.verdict: single-step contact transient while the gate forced the fingers closed on a wedged plate; not a sustained crushing load, no plate destruction, run continued
g2_spike_forensics_20261118.safety_fix: guard must latch on pad channels 12/13 and gripper 16 (peak >500 N abort, >100 N for >=2 frames suspend), plus blocked-open duration cap; verify with offline injection before further real runs

semantics_validated.note: joint_cmd is the expert target opening in the same units and time base as the measured opening; the candidate label can therefore be built from it

gripper_label_candidate_20261118.candidate_rule: err=joint_cmd-opening; err<-0.02 close(+1), >+0.02 open(-1), else hold; minimum hold 3 frames
gripper_label_candidate_20261118.acceptance: the candidate removes ~90% of label chatter while preserving every large-amplitude transition and every long close run; it is a valid supervision candidate, not yet a proven better target
